title: "Lecture 58 — Self-check answers"
sidebar: mfml
---

1. $\alpha_m=\frac12\log\frac{1-\varepsilon_m}{\varepsilon_m}$.
2. Their weights are multiplied by $e^{\alpha_m}$ (then all weights are renormalized).
3. $\hat{y}(x)=\mathrm{sign}\bigl(\sum_m\alpha_m G_m(x)\bigr)$.
4. So $\alpha_m>0$ and the weak learner is better than chance under the current weights.
5. Exponential loss $\ell(y,F)=\exp(-yF)$.
